import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Identify strong features (p < 0.01) based on t-test
    strong_indices = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'expression':
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, i][feats.y==1], feats.x[:, i][feats.y==0])
            if p_val < 0.01:
                strong_indices.append(i)
    
    # If no strong features, return empty design
    if not strong_indices:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=feats.ids, products=(), loadings={fid: 1.0 for fid in feats.ids})
    
    # Compute correlation matrix for strong features
    X_strong = feats.x[:, strong_indices]
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(X_strong.T)
    
    # Cluster correlated features using hierarchical clustering
    clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=None, distance_threshold=0.6, linkage='average')
    clusters = clustering.fit_predict(corr_matrix)
    
    # Select representative features from each cluster
    selected_features = []
    for c in set(clusters):
        cluster_indices = [strong_indices[i] for i in range(len(strong_indices)) if clusters[i] == c]
        cluster_fids = [feats.ids[i] for i in cluster_indices]
        # Choose the feature with highest absolute t-statistic as representative
        best_fid = max(cluster_fids, key=lambda fid: abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], feats.y).statistic))
        selected_features.append(best_fid)
    
    # Sort by effect size
    selected_features.sort(key=lambda fid: abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], feats.y).statistic), reverse=True)
    
    # Return top features as drivers
    drivers = tuple(selected_features[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    columns = tuple(feats.ids)
    products = ()
    loadings = {fid: 1.0 for fid in feats.ids}
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
